title: Purifying a Mixture with Green Chemistry
description: Devise and obtain approval for a method to determine the relative amounts of sodium bicarbonate and sodium carbonate by selective thermal decomposition, collect constant-mass evidence, recover materials separately, calculate composition, and review one teacher-assigned report.
audience: Chemistry students preparing for or reflecting on Mixture Purification
learningGoals: Design and justify an approved gravimetric method based on selective thermal decomposition.
Use lid-askew heating, tongs, cooling, and one balance to establish constant mass safely.
Determine mixture composition from the balanced decomposition stoichiometry and recorded mass loss.
Evaluate scientific quality, reporting quality, atom economy, and another green-chemistry principle in a teacher-provided report.
safetyNotes: Execution remains locked until a teacher approves the proposed method and safety precautions.
Never ignite a burner under a fully covered crucible; keep the lid askew with a visible vent gap.
Move a hot or warm crucible with crucible tongs and cool it at the teacher-configured heat-safe location.
Never place a hot crucible on a balance; heat can damage the instrument and convection can make readings falsely low.
Use the same balance for the empty, loaded, and every cooled-cycle mass.
Follow teacher-configured baseline PPE and local safety rules.
Keep unheated mixture and heated product in their separately labeled recovery containers.
